thien_xu: Thiên Xu Tông, the Pivot: plain undyed grey wool-and-silk robes, the colour of the old bridge stone, matte, well pressed, crossed collar, straight narrow cut, no embroidery and no ornament. Inner disciples wear a black cord with seven small knots tied round the waist. Elders wear a small silver star pinned at the collar. The head alone wears a palm-sized grey stone seal on a cord at the chest. Hair is worn up in a plain knot with a dark wood or iron pin. No instruments, no music, no bright colour; the grey is the uniform and it is always clean.
nhan_van: Nhàn Vân Quán, the abbey of painters: undyed grey silk robes, soft and fine, with the cuffs and sleeve ends stained solid black with ink from work. Hair is knotted up and pinned with a painter's brush, the head's brush being the oldest. Painters of the Pool House wear a thin blue thread at the collar. A little ink, a smear of pigment on a finger or sleeve is normal. Plain, calm, unornamented, cloud-pale.
da_quang: Dạ Quang Môn, former desert raiders turned escorts: riding coats of thick undyed brown-and-grey felt, split for the saddle, with a high leather-edged collar and a wide leather belt; sabres worn on the belt; baggy trousers tucked into tall riding boots; a dust scarf at the neck. Every rider owns one night-glowing cup of pale green jade (the poorer ones of clear glass) carried on a cord at the hip or in the hand. The first blade (the old riders and the elite) wear a red wool band on the upper arm. Young blades add a red cord or tassel. Clothes are fine felt, clean and well kept; plain, never ragged.
tran_sa: Trấn Sa Đường, caravan guards: long dust cloaks the colour of dry sand, hooded or with a high collar, clean and well cut over a plain dark-brown tunic with crossed collar and leather vambraces; a sabre worn on the LEFT hip; a small horn whistle on a cord at the chest. Hair tied back plainly. Smiths of the forge wear a thick leather apron and sleeves instead of the cloak, with no eyebrows (shaved or burnt off). Colours: sand, ochre, dark brown, iron grey; no ornament but the sabre and the whistle.
